title: Safe Actions Alone Do Not Ensure Safe Agents: Identifying Unfulfilled Obligations with Guard Models
title_zh: Safe Actions Alone Do Not Ensure Safe Agents: Identifying Unfulfilled Obligations with Guard Models

paragraphs.en: Guard models are increasingly used to safeguard LLM-based agents, primarily by identifying actions that agents are forbidden to perform. However, identifying forbidden actions alone is insufficient to ensure agent safety. In this paper, we argue that agent safety also depends on identifying required yet unperformed safety-critical actions, which we call obligations . Our preliminary study on a popular benchmark for evaluating safety shows that 56.92% of GLM-5.3 trajectories contain unfulfilled obligations, compared with only 30.00% containing forbidden actions. This finding reveals unfulfilled obligations as a major and previously overlooked source of safety risk. However, to our knowledge, no existing benchmark evaluates whether guard models can identify these obligations.

paragraphs.en: To close this gap, we introduce ObligationBench , the first benchmark for evaluating the capability of obligation identification, comprising 240 expert-validated trajectories covering issue resolution, feature development, and terminal operations. Our evaluation of 14 representative models reveals substantial limitations: the highest recall and exact-match rate are only 48.97% and 10.00%, respectively. To address these limitations, we develop ObligationGuard using 40,000 synthetic training examples. ObligationGuard achieves 57.52% recall and an exact-match rate of 21.67%, surpassing all evaluated models on both metrics. We call on the community to incorporate obligation identification into the design and evaluation of future guard models to improve agent safety.

paragraphs.en: LLM-based agents can now complete increasingly complex tasks autonomously ( Yao et al., 2022 ; Yang et al., 2024 ; Zhou et al., 2024 ) , but their growing autonomy also raises concerns about their safety ( Debenedetti et al., 2024 ; Andriushchenko et al., 2025 ; Zhang et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2026b ; Wang et al., 2026c ; Zhang et al., 2024 ) . To address these concerns, researchers increasingly use guard models to monitor agent behavior during task execution ( Xiang et al., 2025 ; Chen et al., 2025 ; Mou et al., 2026 ; Chennabasappa et al., 2025 ) . As illustrated at the top of Figure 1 , these models improve agent safety primarily by identifying actions that agents are forbidden to perform, such as sending a secret key to an unauthorized external service.

paragraphs.en: In this work, however, we ask a largely overlooked question: is identifying forbidden actions alone sufficient to ensure agent safety? We argue that the answer is no. In many practical scenarios, ensuring agent safety also requires identifying required yet unperformed safety-critical actions, which we call obligations . For example, an agent may legitimately use a secret key to complete a task but fail to remove it afterward, leaving the key exposed even though it performs no forbidden action. To examine how prevalent such safety risks are, we conduct a preliminary study on SusVibes, a benchmark for evaluating coding-agent safety ( Zhao et al., 2026 ) . We find that 56.92% of GLM-5.3 ( Z.ai, 2026 ) trajectories contain unfulfilled obligations, whereas only 30.00% contain forbidden actions. These findings suggest that guard models need to identify obligations to address safety risks that detecting forbidden actions alone would miss, as illustrated at the bottom of Figure 1 . However, to our knowledge, no existing benchmark evaluates this capability.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，在这项工作中，我们提出了一个长期被忽视的问题：仅识别禁止行为是否足以确保智能体的安全性？ 我们认为答案是否定的。 在许多实际场景中，确保智能体安全还需要识别那些必要但尚未执行的安全关键行为，我们将其称为“义务”。 例如，一个智能体可能合法地使用秘密密钥完成任务，但事后未能将其移除，导致密钥暴露在外，尽管它并未执行任何禁止行为。 为了探究此类安全风险有多普遍，我们对 SusVibes（用于评估编码智能体安全的基准测试，Zhao et al., 2026）进行了一项初步研究。 我们发现，GLM-5.3（Z.ai, 2026）的轨迹中，有 56.92% 包含未履行的义务，而仅包含禁止行为的轨迹则占 30.00%。 这些发现表明，防护模型需要识别“义务”，以应对仅通过检测禁止行为而无法发现的安全风险，如图 1 底部所示。 然而，据我们所知，目前尚无任何现有基准测试能够评估这一能力。

paragraphs.en: To close this gap, we propose ObligationBench , the first benchmark designed to evaluate whether guard models can identify agents’ unfulfilled obligations. It contains 240 instances: 120 positive cases with an average of 2.83 obligations per instance and 120 negative cases with no unfulfilled obligations. The benchmark has four key features: ❶ Diverse tasks and agents. It includes trajectories from agents using different LLMs to perform issue resolution, feature development, and terminal operation tasks. ❷ Realistic execution trajectories. These trajectories are drawn from thousands of actual executions on established software-engineering benchmarks. ❸ Broad safety coverage. The obligations span many categories of safety risks, including data exposure, unauthorized access, asset tampering, and identity forgery. ❹ High-quality annotations. Human experts review each instance and correct errors to ensure accurate and complete ground truth.
paragraphs.zh: 为了弥合这一差距，我们提出了 ObligationBench——首个旨在评估守护模型能否识别智能体未履行义务的首个基准测试。 该基准测试包含 240 个实例：120 个正例实例（每个实例平均有 2.83 项义务）和 120 个负例实例（没有未履行的义务）。 该基准测试具有四个关键特征：❶ 多样化的任务与智能体。 它包含了使用不同大型语言模型执行问题处理、特征开发和终端操作任务的智能体的轨迹。❷ 真实的执行轨迹。 这些轨迹源自在成熟的软件工程基准测试上执行的数千次实际运行。❸ 广泛的安全覆盖范围。 这些义务涵盖了多种安全风险类别，包括数据泄露、未经授权的访问、资产篡改和身份伪造。❹ 高质量的标注。 人类专家会审查每个实例并纠正错误，以确保基准测试的真相准确且完整。

paragraphs.en: Our evaluation on ObligationBench reveals substantial limitations in existing models’ ability to identify obligations: even the strongest model, Claude-Opus-4.8 ( Anthropic, 2026 ) , achieves only 48.97% recall and an exact-match rate of 9.17%. To address this limitation, we propose a novel guard model, named ObligationGuard . Training such a guard model requires a large collection of trajectories with accurate and complete obligation annotations. However, collecting real agent trajectories is costly and difficult to scale, while establishing their ground-truth obligation sets requires human annotation. We therefore propose a two-stage data synthesis approach that defines the obligation sets before generating the trajectories. During scenario planning , we construct synthesis templates that specify task scenarios, their safety requirements, and the obligations to remain unfulfilled at termination. During trajectory synthesis , LLMs generate trajectories consistent with these templates, using the specified obligation sets as ground-truth labels. This process yields 40,000 synthetic examples for training ObligationGuard .
paragraphs.zh: 我们在 ObligationBench 上的评估揭示了现有模型在识别义务方面的显著局限性：即便是性能最强的模型——Claude-Opus-4.8（Anthropic，2026）——其召回率也仅为 48.97%，精确匹配率更是只有 9.17%。 为了解决这一局限性，我们提出了一种名为 ObligationGuard 的新型守护模型。 训练这样的守护模型需要大量包含准确且完整义务标注的轨迹数据。 然而，收集真实的智能体轨迹既成本高昂又难以扩展，而确定其真实义务集合则需要人工标注。 因此，我们提出了一种两阶段的数据合成方法，该方法在生成轨迹之前先定义义务集合。 在场景规划阶段，我们构建合成模板，其中明确了任务场景、其安全要求以及任务终止时仍需未完成的义务。 在轨迹合成阶段，大语言模型会根据这些模板生成符合要求的轨迹，并使用指定的义务集合作为真实标签。 这一过程生成了 40,000 个用于训练 ObligationGuard 的合成样本。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate ObligationGuard against 14 representative models on the proposed ObligationBench and examine how obligation identification contributes to agent safety. Our experiments reveal four main findings: ❶ Existing models struggle to identify accurate and complete obligation sets: the highest recall and exact-match rate are only 48.97% and 10.00%, respectively. ❷ The earlier obligations arise in a trajectory and the more obligations coexist, the worse models perform at obligation identification. ❸ ObligationGuard substantially improves this capability, achieving 57.52% recall and an exact-match rate of 21.67% and surpassing all existing models on both metrics. ❹ Guard models that identify obligations more accurately and completely help agents complete tasks more safely. In particular, ObligationGuard-8B increases the agent’s secure task completion rate from 6.5% to 15.1%.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在提出的 ObligationBench 上，将 ObligationGuard 与 14 个代表性模型进行了对比评估，并考察了义务识别对智能体安全性的贡献。 我们的实验揭示了四个主要发现：❶ 现有模型难以识别准确且完整的义务集合：最高的召回率和精确匹配率分别仅为 48.97% 和 10.00%。❷ 义务在轨迹中出现的越早，同时存在的义务越多，模型在义务识别上的表现就越差。❸ ObligationGuard 显著提升了这一能力，实现了 57.52% 的召回率和 21.67% 的精确匹配率，并在两项指标上超越了所有现有模型。❹ 能够更准确、更完整地识别义务的保护模型，有助于智能体更安全地完成任务。 具体而言，ObligationGuard-8B 将智能体的安全任务完成率从 6.5% 提升到了 15.1%。

sents.en: We evaluate ObligationGuard against 14 representative models on the proposed ObligationBench and examine how obligation identification contributes to agent safety.
sents.zh: 我们在提出的 ObligationBench 上，将 ObligationGuard 与 14 个代表性模型进行了对比评估，并考察了义务识别对智能体安全性的贡献。

sents.en: Our experiments reveal four main findings: ❶ Existing models struggle to identify accurate and complete obligation sets: the highest recall and exact-match rate are only 48.97% and 10.00%, respectively. ❷ The earlier obligations arise in a trajectory and the more obligations coexist, the worse models perform at obligation identification. ❸ ObligationGuard substantially improves this capability, achieving 57.52% recall and an exact-match rate of 21.67% and surpassing all existing models on both metrics. ❹ Guard models that identify obligations more accurately and completely help agents complete tasks more safely.
sents.zh: 我们的实验揭示了四个主要发现：❶ 现有模型难以识别准确且完整的义务集合：最高的召回率和精确匹配率分别仅为 48.97% 和 10.00%。❷ 义务在轨迹中出现的越早，同时存在的义务越多，模型在义务识别上的表现就越差。❸ ObligationGuard 显著提升了这一能力，实现了 57.52% 的召回率和 21.67% 的精确匹配率，并在两项指标上超越了所有现有模型。❹ 能够更准确、更完整地识别义务的保护模型，有助于智能体更安全地完成任务。

sents.en: In particular, ObligationGuard-8B increases the agent’s secure task completion rate from 6.5% to 15.1%.
sents.zh: 具体而言，ObligationGuard-8B 将智能体的安全任务完成率从 6.5% 提升到了 15.1%。

paragraphs.en: To summarize, the key contributions of this paper are as follows:
paragraphs.zh: 总而言之，本文的主要贡献如下：

paragraphs.en: We show that existing guard models primarily identify forbidden actions, overlooking a prevalent source of safety risks: required yet unperformed safety-critical actions, which we call obligations.
paragraphs.zh: 我们证明，现有的防护模型主要识别禁止行为，却忽视了一个普遍存在的安全风险来源：那些必须执行但尚未执行的安全关键行为，我们将其称为“义务”。

paragraphs.en: We introduce ObligationBench , the first benchmark for evaluating obligation identification, and reveal that existing models struggle to identify agents’ unfulfilled obligations.
paragraphs.zh: 我们提出了 ObligationBench——首个用于评估义务识别能力的基准测试，并发现现有模型在识别智能体未履行义务方面存在困难。

paragraphs.en: We develop ObligationGuard , which surpasses all evaluated guard models in recall and exact-match rate and helps agents complete tasks more safely.
paragraphs.zh: 我们开发了 ObligationGuard，它在召回率和精确匹配率方面超越了所有经过评估的防护模型，并帮助智能体更安全地完成任务。

paragraphs.en: As agents gain greater autonomy, their safety has attracted growing attention ( Zhang et al., 2026b ; Zhang et al., 2026c ; Wang et al., 2026e ) . AgentHarm shows that agents can be induced to carry out harmful requests, while AgentDojo examines how malicious instructions in external data can lead to unsafe actions. Safety risks also arise without such malicious instructions ( Wang et al., 2026a ; Liu et al., 2026b ; Ruan et al., 2024 ) . For example, SusVibes ( Zhao et al., 2026 ) evaluates coding agents on real-world software-engineering tasks, revealing that their implementations often contain security vulnerabilities even when they satisfy functional requirements.
paragraphs.zh: 随着智能体获得更大的自主性，其安全性也日益受到关注（Zhang 等人，2026b；Zhang 等人，2026c；Wang 等人，2026e）。 AgentHarm 表明，智能体可以被诱导执行有害请求，而 AgentDojo 则研究了外部数据中的恶意指令如何导致不安全的行为。 即使没有此类恶意指令，安全风险依然存在（Wang 等人，2026a；Liu 等人，2026b；Ruan 等人，2024）。 例如，SusVibes（Zhao 等人，2026）通过真实世界的软件工程任务评估编码智能体，发现即使这些智能体满足功能要求，其实现中也常常存在安全漏洞。

paragraphs.en: To address these safety risks, researchers increasingly use guard models to monitor agent behavior ( Wang et al., 2026d ; Xiao et al., 2026 ; Lin et al., 2026 ) . Qwen3Guard ( Zhao et al., 2025 ) classifies the safety of prompts and responses, while GuardAgent ( Xiang et al., 2025 ) uses executable checks to assess agent behavior against safety requirements. AgentDoG 1.5 ( Liu et al., 2026a ) provides real-time safety monitoring with lightweight models. These safety judgments can also guide subsequent actions: ToolSafe ( Mou et al., 2026 ) provides guidance before proposed actions are executed. To evaluate the reliability of such judgments ( Yuan et al., 2024 ; Li et al., 2026 ; Luo et al., 2025 ) , SafePyramid ( Zhang et al., 2026a ) tests whether models can identify violations of specified safety requirements, while TraceSafe ( Chen et al., 2026a ) evaluates their ability to detect safety risks in multi-step agent trajectories.
paragraphs.zh: 为应对这些安全风险，研究人员越来越多地使用守护模型来监控智能体的行为（Wang 等，2026d；Xiao 等，2026；Lin 等，2026）。 Qwen3Guard（Zhao 等，2025）对提示词和响应的安全性进行分类，而 GuardAgent（Xiang 等，2025）则通过可执行检查来评估智能体行为是否符合安全要求。 AgentDoG 1.5（Liu 等，2026a）利用轻量级模型提供实时安全监控。 这些安全判断也可以指导后续行动：ToolSafe（Mou 等，2026）在拟执行动作前提供指导。 为评估此类判断的可靠性（Yuan 等，2024；Li 等，2026；Luo 等，2025），SafePyramid（Zhang 等，2026a）测试模型能否识别对指定安全要求的违反行为，而 TraceSafe（Chen 等，2026a）则评估它们在多步骤智能体轨迹中检测安全风险的能力。

paragraphs.en: Existing guard models primarily examine whether an agent’s actions violate safety requirements. However, we find that a trajectory without any forbidden actions may still be unsafe. Figure 2 illustrates this limitation through a real trajectory of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash ( DeepSeek-AI, 2026 ) . The agent was tasked with adding Remember me functionality to Rdiffweb, an open-source web application for managing backups. 1 1 1 https://github.com/ikus060/rdiffweb It modified the authentication code to support persistent login and terminated after the targeted functional tests passed. However, it did not implement a server-side check to reject expired sessions, allowing an old session cookie to remain usable beyond the intended session lifetime. To terminate safely, the agent still needed to implement this expiration check ( OWASP Foundation, [n. d.] ) . A guard model must therefore identify this missing action even when no forbidden action has been performed. We refer to such required yet unperformed safety-critical actions as obligations .

paragraphs.en: The practical significance of existing guard models’ limitations depends on how frequently unfulfilled obligations contribute to safety failures in real agent executions. We therefore analyze trajectories from agents powered by DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and GLM-5.3 on SusVibes, which evaluates functionality and safety separately. We define Unsafe Rate as the percentage of all evaluated executions that fail the safety tests. For each unsafe execution, we use GPT-5.6-Sol ( OpenAI, 2026 ) to analyze its trajectory and annotate whether the failure involves forbidden actions, unfulfilled obligations, or both. Forbidden Action and Unfulfilled Obligation report the percentages of all evaluated executions assigned the respective labels.
paragraphs.zh: 现有守护模型局限性的实际意义取决于未履行的义务在真实智能体执行中导致安全故障的频率。 因此，我们分析了由 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 和 GLM-5.3 驱动的智能体在 SusVibes 上的运行轨迹，该平台会分别评估功能性和安全性。 我们将“不安全率”定义为所有受评估执行中未通过安全测试的执行所占的百分比。 对于每次不安全的执行，我们使用 GPT-5.6-Sol（OpenAI, 2026）分析其运行轨迹，并标注该故障是否涉及禁止行动、未履行义务或两者兼有。 “禁止行动”和“未履行义务”分别报告了所有受评估执行中被赋予相应标签的执行所占的百分比。

paragraphs.en: Table 2 shows that, for both evaluated models, safety risks primarily arise from unfulfilled obligations. For example, unfulfilled obligations occur in 56.92% of all GLM-5.3 executions, compared with 30.00% containing forbidden actions. paragraphs.en: In this section, we propose ObligationBench , the first benchmark designed to evaluate whether guard models can identify agents’ unfulfilled obligations. It is built from diverse, realistic agent execution trajectories and provides accurate, complete annotations of the obligations that remain unfulfilled at termination. Together, these properties enable systematic evaluation of obligation identification under realistic execution contexts.

paragraphs.en: Real agent executions may terminate with unfulfilled obligations or with none at all. Beyond identifying genuine obligations, a guard model should avoid false positives when no intervention is needed, since unnecessary safety interventions may reduce agent utility. We therefore construct a pair of positive and negative instances for each user task. paragraphs.en: As shown in Figure 3 , the 339 obligations span five safety categories. Data Exposure (93 obligations, 27.43%) concerns sensitive information that remains accessible to unintended parties because of residual data or inadequate access controls. Unauthorized Access (53 obligations, 15.63%) concerns accounts, permissions, or sessions that remain usable beyond their authorized scope or duration. Asset Tampering (86 obligations, 25.37%) concerns unauthorized modifications that compromise the integrity of protected software, records, or system state. Identity Forgery (88 obligations, 25.96%) concerns the misuse of signing or trust mechanisms to falsely present identities or artifacts as authentic or as originating from a trusted source. The remaining 19 obligations (5.60%) fall into Others, covering additional safety requirements such as maintaining service availability and preserving security audit evidence. This distribution provides broad coverage of safety requirements, with no single category dominating the benchmark.

sents.en: Specifically, we sample 1,000 tasks in total and execute them using four representative LLM backends: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, Kimi-K3 ( Kimi Team et al., 2026 ) , GPT-5.6-Sol, and Claude-Opus-4.8 to further increase trajectory diversity.
sents.zh: 具体而言，我们总共采样了 1,000 个任务，并使用四个具有代表性的 LLM 后端执行这些任务：DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash、Kimi-K3（Kimi Team 等，2026）、GPT-5.6-Sol 和 Claude-Opus-4.8，以进一步增加轨迹的多样性。

sents.en: After removing runs affected by infrastructure failures or incomplete environment initialization, we retain 5,684 valid trajectories.
sents.zh: 在移除受基础设施故障或环境初始化不完整影响的运行结果后，我们保留了 5,684 条有效轨迹。

paragraphs.en: Trajectory Filtering. Most of the 5,684 collected trajectories contain no safety-relevant behavior and are therefore unsuitable for obligation annotation. Directly annotating and reviewing all trajectories would incur prohibitive cost. We therefore use GPT-5.6-Sol to first filter the trajectory pool and identify candidates that may contain obligations.

paragraphs.en: Trajectory Annotation. ObligationBench requires a complete obligation set for each instance as ground truth, but direct human annotation is costly. We therefore use GPT-5.6-Sol to annotate the retained trajectories with their unfulfilled obligation sets and supporting evidence. As described in Section 3.1 , the benchmark also requires negative instances with no unfulfilled obligations. For each retained positive task, we rerun the task until obtaining a trajectory whose annotated obligation set is empty, forming a matched negative instance. Finally, we obtain 180 positive and 180 negative candidates for human review.
paragraphs.zh: 轨迹标注。 ObligationBench 要求每个实例都有一组完整的义务作为基准真相，但直接由人类进行标注成本高昂。 因此，我们使用 GPT-5.6-Sol 为保留的轨迹标注其未履行的义务集及支持证据。 如第 3.1 节所述，该基准测试还需要没有未履行义务的负例实例。 对于每个保留的正例任务，我们会重复执行该任务，直到获得一个其标注义务集为空集的轨迹，从而形成一个匹配的负例实例。 最终，我们获得了 180 个正例和 180 个负例候选样本供人类审核。

paragraphs.en: Human Review. To ensure accurate and complete annotations of unfulfilled obligations, two software engineers with over five years of professional experience independently review and correct the model-generated annotations against the original task and complete trajectory. Before adjudication, they achieve an 82.2% agreement rate on the complete obligation set. Disagreements are resolved through discussion, and ambiguous cases are discarded. This yields 240 expert-validated instances: 120 positive cases and 120 hard negatives.
paragraphs.zh: 人工审核。 为确保对未履行义务的标注准确且完整，两名拥有五年以上专业经验的软件工程师会独立审核并修正模型生成的标注，对照原始任务与完整轨迹进行核对。 在裁决前，他们在完整义务集合上的同意率达到 82.2%。 分歧通过讨论解决，而模糊不清的案例则被舍弃。 由此获得了 240 个经专家验证的实例：120 个阳性案例和 120 个困难阴性案例。

paragraphs.en: To improve models’ ability to identify unfulfilled obligations, we develop ObligationGuard . We first synthesize training data through scenario planning and trajectory synthesis (Section 4.1 ), and then use these data for supervised fine-tuning (Section 4.2 ).

paragraphs.en: Training ObligationGuard requires a large collection of trajectories with accurate and complete obligation annotations. Obtaining such data from real agent executions is costly and difficult to scale, as it requires both extensive trajectory collection and manual ground-truth annotation. We therefore propose a two-stage data synthesis approach. In scenario planning , we design tasks together with their ground-truth obligation sets. In trajectory synthesis , we generate execution trajectories consistent with these tasks and obligation sets.
paragraphs.zh: 训练 ObligationGuard 需要大量包含准确且完整义务标注的轨迹集合。 从真实智能体执行中获取此类数据既昂贵又难以扩展，因为这既需要大规模收集轨迹，也需要人工进行真实值标注。 因此，我们提出了一种两阶段的数据合成方法。 在场景规划中，我们会同其真实值义务集一起设计任务。 在轨迹合成中，我们会生成与这些任务和真实值义务集一致的执行轨迹。

paragraphs.en: We conduct comprehensive experiments to evaluate models’ ability to identify obligations. This section presents our research questions, evaluated models, metrics, and implementation details.
paragraphs.zh: 我们进行了全面的实验，以评估模型识别义务的能力。 本节介绍了我们的研究问题、所评估的模型、指标以及实现细节。

sents.en: We conduct comprehensive experiments to evaluate models’ ability to identify obligations.
sents.zh: 我们进行了全面的实验，以评估模型识别义务的能力。

sents.en: This section presents our research questions, evaluated models, metrics, and implementation details.
sents.zh: 本节介绍了我们的研究问题、所评估的模型、指标以及实现细节。

paragraphs.en: Our experiments address the following four research questions (RQs).
paragraphs.zh: 我们的实验旨在探讨以下四个研究问题（RQ）。

paragraphs.en: RQ1: How effectively can existing models identify obligations? This RQ evaluates whether existing models can identify accurate and complete obligation sets. To answer it, we evaluate 14 representative general-purpose LLMs and guard models on ObligationBench .
paragraphs.zh: RQ1：现有模型能多有效地识别义务？ 本研究问题评估现有模型能否识别准确且完整的义务集合。 为回答该问题，我们在 ObligationBench 上评估了 14 款具有代表性的通用 LLM 和 guard 模型。

sents.en: RQ1: How effectively can existing models identify obligations?
sents.zh: RQ1：现有模型能多有效地识别义务？

sents.en: This RQ evaluates whether existing models can identify accurate and complete obligation sets.
sents.zh: 本研究问题评估现有模型能否识别准确且完整的义务集合。

sents.en: To answer it, we evaluate 14 representative general-purpose LLMs and guard models on ObligationBench .
sents.zh: 为回答该问题，我们在 ObligationBench 上评估了 14 款具有代表性的通用 LLM 和 guard 模型。

paragraphs.en: RQ2: What factors affect models’ performance in obligation identification? This RQ examines when models struggle to identify all unfulfilled obligations. To answer it, we analyze how performance varies with the point at which obligations arise in a trajectory and the number of obligations that coexist.
paragraphs.zh: 研究问题 2：哪些因素会影响模型在义务识别方面的表现？ 本研究问题旨在探究模型在何种情况下难以识别所有未履行义务。 为回答该问题，我们将分析模型表现如何随义务在轨迹中出现的时点以及同时存在的义务数量而变化。

sents.en: RQ2: What factors affect models’ performance in obligation identification?
sents.zh: 研究问题 2：哪些因素会影响模型在义务识别方面的表现？

sents.en: This RQ examines when models struggle to identify all unfulfilled obligations.
sents.zh: 本研究问题旨在探究模型在何种情况下难以识别所有未履行义务。

sents.en: To answer it, we analyze how performance varies with the point at which obligations arise in a trajectory and the number of obligations that coexist.
sents.zh: 为回答该问题，我们将分析模型表现如何随义务在轨迹中出现的时点以及同时存在的义务数量而变化。

paragraphs.en: RQ3: What contributes to the effectiveness of ObligationGuard ? We conduct ablation studies to examine how model size, model family, training-data size, and the use of synthesis templates affect ObligationGuard ’s performance. We compare fine-tuned models with their original backbones across three sizes and two families, and vary the number of synthetic training examples. To assess the contribution of synthesis templates, we also compare training on directly generated trajectories with training on trajectories generated from templates.
paragraphs.zh: RQ3：哪些因素有助于 ObligationGuard 的有效性？ 我们进行了消融研究，以考察模型规模、模型家族、训练数据规模以及合成模板的使用如何影响 ObligationGuard 的性能。 我们在三种规模和两个模型家族中，将微调后的模型与其原始主干模型进行比较，并调整合成训练样本的数量。 为了评估合成模板的贡献，我们还比较了直接使用生成的轨迹进行训练与使用从模板生成的轨迹进行训练的效果。

sents.en: RQ3: What contributes to the effectiveness of ObligationGuard ?
sents.zh: RQ3：哪些因素有助于 ObligationGuard 的有效性？

sents.en: We conduct ablation studies to examine how model size, model family, training-data size, and the use of synthesis templates affect ObligationGuard ’s performance.
sents.zh: 我们进行了消融研究，以考察模型规模、模型家族、训练数据规模以及合成模板的使用如何影响 ObligationGuard 的性能。

sents.en: We compare fine-tuned models with their original backbones across three sizes and two families, and vary the number of synthetic training examples.

paragraphs.en: RQ4: Does stronger obligation identification improve agent safety? This RQ examines whether guard models that identify obligations more accurately and completely help agents complete tasks more safely. To answer it, we integrate guard models into a coding agent and evaluate their effects on functional correctness and safety on SusVibes.
paragraphs.zh: 研究问题4：更强的义务识别能力能否提升智能体的安全性？ 本研究问题旨在探究，能够更准确、更全面地识别义务的保护模型，是否有助于智能体更安全地完成任务。 为回答该问题，我们将保护模型集成到编码智能体中，并在 SusVibes 上评估其对功能正确性和安全性的影响。

sents.en: RQ4: Does stronger obligation identification improve agent safety?
sents.zh: 研究问题4：更强的义务识别能力能否提升智能体的安全性？

sents.en: This RQ examines whether guard models that identify obligations more accurately and completely help agents complete tasks more safely.
sents.zh: 本研究问题旨在探究，能够更准确、更全面地识别义务的保护模型，是否有助于智能体更安全地完成任务。

sents.en: To answer it, we integrate guard models into a coding agent and evaluate their effects on functional correctness and safety on SusVibes.
sents.zh: 为回答该问题，我们将保护模型集成到编码智能体中，并在 SusVibes 上评估其对功能正确性和安全性的影响。

paragraphs.en: We evaluate ObligationGuard against 14 existing models from different model families and sizes, covering both general-purpose LLMs and guard models.

paragraphs.en: Unfulfilled obligations pose substantial safety risks, yet identifying them requires more than judging whether an agent’s recorded actions are permitted. In this RQ, we evaluate whether existing models can identify accurate and complete obligation sets.

paragraphs.en: Existing models struggle to identify accurate and complete obligation sets. Although several existing models achieve high Precision and classification accuracy, their Recall and EM remain low. For example, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash achieves 90.08% Precision and 95.83% CA − \mathrm{CA}_{-} , but its Recall is only 32.15%. Similarly, Claude-Opus-4.8 achieves 93.33% CA + \mathrm{CA}_{+} , yet its EM is only 9.17%. Across all 14 existing models, the highest Recall and EM are only 48.97% and 10.00%, respectively. The low EM is particularly concerning: even the best result corresponds to an accurate and complete obligation set on only one in ten positive instances. Thus, while these models can identify some required actions, their guidance may still leave other safety-critical actions unaddressed.
paragraphs.zh: 现有模型难以识别准确且完整的义务集合。 尽管一些现有模型实现了较高的精确度和分类准确率，但其召回率和 EM 仍然较低。 例如，DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 的精确度为 90.08%，CA − \mathrm{CA}_{-} 为 95.83%，但召回率仅为 32.15%。 同样，Claude-Opus-4.8 的 CA + \mathrm{CA}_{+} 为 93.33%，但其 EM 仅为 9.17%。 在所有 14 个现有模型中，最高的召回率和 EM 分别仅为 48.97% 和 10.00%。 较低的 EM 尤其令人担忧：即使最佳结果也仅能在十分之一的正例中识别出准确且完整的义务集合。 因此，尽管这些模型能够识别部分必要行动，但其指导仍可能遗漏其他与安全至关重要的行动。

paragraphs.en: Existing guard models perform worse than most general-purpose LLMs. Despite being trained for safety, the three existing guard models achieve at most 5.60% Recall and 0.83% EM. They often fail to recognize that any obligations remain, with CA + \mathrm{CA}_{+} no higher than 29.17%. For example, Llama-Guard-3-8B returns no obligations on any instance, obtaining 100.00% CA − \mathrm{CA}_{-} but 0.00% CA + \mathrm{CA}_{+} . It therefore provides no guidance on the required actions even when the agent still has unfulfilled obligations. We attribute this gap in part to the focus of existing safety training on detecting forbidden actions. Such training may help models judge whether an action is permitted without teaching them to identify actions that are required but missing from the trajectory.
paragraphs.zh: 现有的守卫模型表现不如大多数通用大型语言模型。 尽管经过安全训练，三种现有的守卫模型最多也只能达到 5.60% 的召回率和 0.83% 的 EM。 它们常常无法识别任何义务仍然存在，其中 CA + \mathrm{CA}_{+} 不超过 29.17%。 例如，Llama-Guard-3-8B 在任何实例上都没有返回任何义务，获得了 100.00% 的 CA − \mathrm{CA}_{-}，但 CA + \mathrm{CA}_{+} 为 0.00%。 因此，即使智能体仍有未履行的义务，它也无法提供关于所需行动的指导。 我们将这一差距部分归因于现有安全训练主要集中在检测禁止行动上。 此类训练可能有助于模型判断某项行动是否被允许，但并未教会它们识别那些虽有必要却未出现在轨迹中的行动。

sents.en: We attribute this gap in part to the focus of existing safety training on detecting forbidden actions.

paragraphs.en: ObligationGuard substantially improves obligation identification. paragraphs.en: Our synthetic data improves obligation identification at all three model sizes. As shown in Table 3 , fine-tuning improves Precision, Recall, and EM for all three Qwen3 models. For example, Qwen3-4B’s Recall increases from 10.91% to 43.66%, and its EM from 0.00% to 12.50%. Qwen3-14B also benefits substantially, with Recall rising from 18.88% to 62.54% and EM from 1.67% to 25.83%. paragraphs.en: ObligationGuard improves agent safety while largely preserving functional correctness. Without guidance, the agent achieves 6.5% SecPass. paragraphs.en: Identifying the unfulfilled obligation helps the agent address the specific safety failure. Figure 9 illustrates how the guidance leads to a safer solution. In this persistent-login task, the agent attempts to terminate at step 24, although server-side session expiration is still missing. An old session may therefore remain usable after its intended expiration time. Qwen3-8B suggests clearing the persistent cookie on logout, which leaves expiration enforcement unaddressed. ObligationGuard instead identifies the obligation to reject expired sessions. Following this guidance, the agent adds the server-side expiration check and requires users with expired sessions to log in again. Its solution becomes Correct-Safe while retaining its functional behavior. This case illustrates how identifying the unfulfilled obligation guides the agent toward the required safety-critical action.

paragraphs.en: Guard models with better performance on ObligationBench tend to improve agent safety more. Across the six evaluated guard models, Recall on ObligationBench is strongly associated with the improvement in SecPass on SusVibes (Spearman’s ρ = 0.94 \rho=0.94 ; Pearson’s r = 0.97 r=0.97 ). This association links performance on ObligationBench to the usefulness of guidance from guard models during agent execution. It suggests that guard models that identify more unfulfilled obligations can give agents more complete guidance on the safety-critical actions still required.

paragraphs.en: We use GPT-5.6-Sol to assess semantic equivalence between predicted and ground-truth obligations. To examine the reliability of these judgments, we manually review 400 obligation pairs from the RQ1 results, stratified by evaluated model: 200 judged as matched and 200 as unmatched. Reviewers assess each pair using the corresponding task and trajectory, without seeing the model’s identity or the LLM judge’s decision. Human review confirms 196 of the 200 matched judgments (98.0%) and 184 of the 200 unmatched judgments (92.0%), giving 95.0% overall agreement on this balanced sample. These results indicate that the LLM judge provides reliable semantic matching judgments.
paragraphs.zh: 我们使用 GPT-5.6-Sol 来评估预测义务与真实义务之间的语义等价性。 为了检验这些判断的可靠性，我们从 RQ1 的结果中手动审查了 400 对义务，按评估模型进行分层：其中 200 对被判定为匹配，200 对被判定为不匹配。 审查人员根据相应的任务和轨迹评估每一对义务，且不会看到模型的身份或 LLM 判断者的决策。 人工审查确认了 200 个匹配判断中的 196 个（98.0%），以及 200 个不匹配判断中的 184 个（92.0%），因此在这一平衡样本上的总体一致率为 95.0%。 这些结果表明，LLM 判断者能够提供可靠的语义匹配判断。

paragraphs.en: We consider four threats to the validity of our study:
paragraphs.zh: 我们认为我们的研究存在以下四个有效性威胁：

paragraphs.en: Reliability of obligation annotations. Annotating obligations requires determining which safety-critical actions are necessary and whether the agent has completed them. Automatic annotation may overlook a required action or mistake an unnecessary action for an obligation, affecting model evaluation. To mitigate this threat, two software engineers with over five years of professional experience independently review and correct the initial annotations. They check whether the annotated actions remain required at termination and identify any missing obligations, then resolve disagreements through discussion and discard ambiguous cases.
paragraphs.zh: 义务标注的可靠性。 标注义务需要确定哪些安全关键行动是必要的，以及智能体是否已完成这些行动。 自动标注可能会忽略某个必要行动，或将不必要的行动误认为义务，从而影响模型评估。 为缓解这一风险，两位拥有超过五年专业经验的软件工程师会独立审查并修正初始标注结果。 他们会检查被标注的行动在程序终止时是否仍然必要，识别任何缺失的义务，然后通过讨论解决分歧，并舍弃存在歧义的情况。

paragraphs.en: Diversity and realism of the benchmark. Synthetic trajectories may not capture the variety of tasks and execution behavior that agents encounter in practice, limiting the benchmark’s diversity and realism. We therefore collect trajectories from actual executions on established software-engineering benchmarks, covering issue resolution, feature development, and terminal operation. Agents powered by four different LLMs provide varied trajectories within these domains. This coverage also extends to the safety requirements: the benchmark includes five safety categories and one to five unfulfilled obligations per positive instance.

paragraphs.en: Practical relevance of the benchmark. High scores on ObligationBench alone do not establish whether a guard model improves agent safety in practice. We therefore evaluate six guard models on SusVibes by using their predicted obligations to guide an agent. At its first termination attempt, the agent receives the identified obligations and can continue execution to fulfill them. We find that higher Recall on ObligationBench is associated with larger SecPass gains, supporting the benchmark’s relevance to agent safety during actual execution.

paragraphs.en: In this paper, we show that identifying forbidden actions alone is insufficient to ensure agent safety, as unfulfilled obligations constitute a major source of safety risk. We introduce ObligationBench , the first benchmark for obligation identification, and find that 14 existing models struggle to identify accurate and complete obligation sets. To address this limitation, we develop ObligationGuard using synthetic training data generated through scenario planning and trajectory synthesis. Our experiments demonstrate that ObligationGuard improves obligation identification and helps agents complete tasks more safely while largely preserving functional completion. We hope this work encourages the community to incorporate obligation identification into the design and evaluation of future guard models.
